Hi Lisa,

Thanks again for the chat earlier today — appreciated the time. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

Attendees: Lisa Turner (Acme Health), Tom Alvarez (Acme Health), Jonas Weber (Redwood), Vanessa Ortiz (Redwood)

Key pain points / goals:
- Per-customer rate limits: you need strict, per-tenant TPS and token quotas to prevent noisy tenants from degrading service.
- Per-customer routing/policies: ability to route specific tenants to dedicated pools or lower-cost quantized model variants.
- Tiering: you want 3 tiers (Standard/Plus/Priority) with different SLA/throughput targets and quota windows.
- Auditability: retention of per-tenant logs and ability to export usage for billing.

Current stack:
- In-house service proxy + Redis-based quota tracking; occasional cold-start latency spikes when firing up GPU workers.
- Using a mix of open LLMs hosted on cloud VMs via managed infra.

Success criteria (what would be a win):
1) Enforce per-tenant quotas with <5% operational overhead and no cross-tenant interference.
2) Route top-tier tenants to reserved capacity with predictable p99 latency under 300ms for 1k-token requests.
3) Exportable usage/chargeback data with daily granularity and SOC2-friendly logs.

Proposed next steps (owners + dates):
- Technical deep dive on routing & quota ops (Rishi Malhotra, Redwood SE) — schedule for next week (owner: Acme)
- Send proposed SLA matrix + SOC2 summary (owner: Redwood) — I will attach in next email (by EOD tomorrow)
- Mutual action plan + pricing ballpark (owner: Jonas) — deliverable by 05/06/2026

Open questions you flagged:
- Do you expect per-tenant KV cache isolation or shared cache with logical limits?
- Rough monthly tokens per tier (we can propose default quotas once we have ballpark usage).

I'll wait for a proposed time for a 45-minute technical runthrough with your infra/engineering team. Thanks — looking forward to the deep dive.

Hi Lisa/Tom — quick technical notes ahead of the session and attached files.

Key engineering notes:
- Rate limits: we implement per-tenant token and request rate limits at the ingress proxy; hard ceilings enforced in the serving runtime. Dynamic quota updates via control-plane API.
- Routing: tenants carry a routing tag; policy engine can map tags to pools (dedicated/reserved, shared standard, or fallback to cost-optimized variants). We support rule-based and label-based routing.
- Cache isolation: options: per-tenant VM/pool for full isolation (higher cost) or shared pool with per-tenant KV sizing and eviction guarantees (lower cost). We recommend per-tenant isolation for Priority tier, shared+caps for Standard.
- Tiering defaults we typically recommend (can be tuned): Standard: 100 rps burst / 10k tokens/day tenant; Plus: 500 rps / 100k tokens/day; Priority: 2k rps / 1M tokens/day.

Attachments (stubs):
- rwi-sla-matrix.pdf (SLA by tier, latency targets, availability)
